# ibex_cosim_agent Behavioral Specification

## 1. Overview

The `ibex_cosim_agent` is a passive UVM agent used in the Ibex co-simulation verification environment. Its purpose is to collect RTL execution observations and memory interface traffic and make them available to an internal checker that keeps a RISC-V ISS synchronized with the DUT. It also provides direct reference-model memory initialization facilities and a reset operation for the checking path.

The agent shall not generate stimulus. It is responsible for observation, checking-path setup, reference-model memory backdoor writes, and state clearing.

## 2. Interfaces

- The agent shall expose two externally visible analysis exports:
  1. A data-memory interface export, used to accept observed data memory transactions.
  2. An instruction-memory interface export, used to accept observed instruction memory transactions.
- Every transaction item received on either export must be forwarded to the internal checker without being dropped or duplicated.
- Items from each source must be delivered to the checker in the same order in which they are received.

## 3. Observation and Checking Path

The agent shall establish the observation and checking infrastructure needed to support RTL/ISS lockstep co-simulation.

Before simulation traffic begins, the agent must ensure that all internal observation sources and the checker are connected. This includes:

- Retired instruction and synchronous trap information from the RISC-V Formal Interface (RVFI). For every retired or synchronously trapping instruction, the agent shall pass the instruction and register-write information to the checker so that the reference model can be stepped and compared.
- Instruction fetch transaction information. Every observed instruction fetch transaction shall be forwarded to the checker for use in instruction-fetch error tracking and synchronization.
- Instruction-fetch PMP check results. Every observed instruction-fetch PMP outcome shall be forwarded to the checker.
- All data-memory and instruction-memory transactions arriving at the agent’s analysis exports shall be forwarded to the checker for memory access checking and bus-error handling.

The agent shall not make functional checking decisions itself. It shall only transport observations and provide access to the checker’s reset and memory-initialization capabilities.

## 4. Reference-Model Memory Initialization

The agent shall provide mechanisms to initialize the reference model memory directly, without generating bus activity on the DUT.

### Byte write

- A byte-write operation shall accept a 32-bit byte address and an 8-bit data value.
- It shall update the reference model memory at that address with the supplied byte.
- No alignment requirement shall be imposed.

### Word write

- A word-write operation shall accept a 32-bit base address and a data word.
- The word width is the configured data width of the environment.
- The word shall be written as a sequence of bytes to consecutive addresses starting at the base address.
- The least-significant byte of the word shall be written first, followed by successively more significant bytes.
- The sequence shall continue for one byte per 8 bits of the configured word width.

### Binary file load

- A binary-load operation shall accept a 32-bit base address and a binary file path.
- It shall open the file in binary mode and read it from beginning to end.
- Each byte read from the file shall be written to the reference model memory at the current memory address.
- The memory address shall start at the base address and increment by one for every byte read.
- If the file cannot be opened, the agent shall report a fatal error and shall not continue the load operation.
- If the file is empty, no memory writes shall be performed.

## 5. Reset and State Clearing

The agent shall provide a reset operation for the co-simulation checking path.

When invoked, the reset operation must:

- Flush all unprocessed observation items, including RVFI data, data-memory transactions, instruction-memory transactions, instruction-fetch data, and instruction-fetch PMP results.
- Complete the queue flushes before notifying the internal co-simulation scoreboard of the reset.
- Discard all pre-reset observations without checking them against the post-reset ISS state.
- Trigger the scoreboard reset mechanism so that active checking tasks are terminated and the ISS session is reinitialized.

Reinitializing the ISS may discard the existing reference-model memory contents. Therefore, after the ISS has been reinitialized and before post-reset checking resumes, the test binary must be loaded into the new reference-model memory instance again.

# Behavioral Specification: Ibex Co-simulation Scoreboard

## 1. Purpose

The scoreboard is a passive UVM verification component that checks RTL execution of the Ibex core against a RISC-V instruction set simulator (ISS). It observes retired instructions, data-side memory accesses, and instruction-side fetch status from the RTL, and drives the ISS into lockstep so that every architecturally visible RTL action is validated.

The scoreboard must:

- Maintain a co-simulation session with the ISS.
- Check retired instructions against the ISS.
- Forward all data-side memory accesses to the ISS.
- Track instruction-side fetch errors that can produce instruction-fault traps.
- Apply asynchronous events and counter values to the ISS before each instruction is advanced.
- Report mismatches and clean up ISS resources at end of simulation or on abort.

## 2. Configuration and Initialization

The scoreboard must obtain its configuration from the UVM configuration database. If the configuration is unavailable, it must report a fatal error.

Using that configuration, the scoreboard must initialize the ISS with:

- The RISC-V ISA string.
- The initial program counter.
- The initial trap vector.
- The log file destination.
- The number of PMP regions and PMP granularity.
- The number of implemented performance counters.
- Whether the core is in secure mode.
- Whether the instruction cache is present.

Initialization must be performed before checking begins. If the ISS cannot be initialized, the scoreboard must report a fatal error.

The scoreboard must release the ISS session when simulation ends normally and also when simulation terminates early due to an abort. If a reset occurs, the scoreboard must terminate the current checking activity and reinitialize the ISS for a fresh co-simulation session.

## 3. Reset Behavior

The scoreboard shall coordinate reset handling with the explicit reset notification generated by the co-simulation agent.

For each execution interval, the scoreboard shall:

1. Wait for reset to be deasserted before starting the checking tasks.
2. Run the instruction, memory, instruction-fetch, and PMP checking tasks concurrently.
3. Upon receiving a reset notification, terminate all active checking tasks before any post-reset observations are processed.
4. Reinitialize the ISS as a new co-simulation session.
5. Return to waiting for the next reset deassertion before restarting the checking tasks.



No instruction or memory observation from before reset may be checked against the new ISS session. The reset sequence must allow the testbench to reload the test binary into the new ISS memory model before post-reset checking resumes.

## 4. Retired Instruction Checking

For each retired instruction record received from the RTL, the scoreboard must:

1. Discard any pending instruction-side error records for instructions that were fetched but never retired.
2. If the retired instruction has an associated instruction-side fetch error, notify the ISS of the failing instruction address before advancing the ISS.
3. Apply to the ISS the asynchronous state captured with that instruction:
   - Non-maskable interrupt request.
   - Interrupt-pending bits.
   - Debug request.
4. Apply to the ISS the cycle counter value and all performance counter values captured with that instruction.
5. Apply the instruction-cache scramble-key-valid status captured with that instruction.
6. Advance the ISS by one instruction, providing:
   - The destination register number, if any.
   - The register write data, if any.
   - The program counter of the instruction.
   - Whether the instruction caused a synchronous trap.

A synchronously trapping instruction must be presented to the ISS with its trap indication. The ISS must then expect the next instruction to be the first instruction of the trap handler.

If the ISS reports a mismatch, the scoreboard must collect all reported error messages and report them as a single message. After reporting, the error list in the ISS must be cleared.

If relaxed checking is configured, a mismatch must be reported as an informational message and checking may continue. Otherwise, a mismatch must be reported as a fatal error.

## 5. Data-Side Memory Access Notification

Every data-side memory access observed from the RTL must be forwarded to the ISS.

For each access, the scoreboard must provide:

- Whether it is a read or write.
- The accessed address.
- The write data, if any.
- The byte enables.
- Whether the access received an error response.
- Whether the access is the first or second half of a misaligned access.

Data-side access notifications must be delivered to the ISS in the order they are observed. The error status must be included because the ISS uses it to model load/store bus-error traps.

Data-side accesses must be notified before the retired instruction that caused them is advanced in the ISS, so that the ISS can match the accesses and generate the correct trap behavior.

## 6. Instruction-Side Fetch Error Tracking

Instruction-side accesses from Ibex can be speculative, so the scoreboard must not compare them directly with ISS instruction fetches. Instead, it must track only instruction-side fetch errors that can cause an instruction-fault trap.

The scoreboard must support two instruction-side error probing modes, selected by configuration:

- External probing of the instruction memory interface.
- Internal probing of the instruction fetch stage and PMP results.

### 6.1 External Probing Mode

In external probing mode, the scoreboard must observe instruction memory bus transactions.

- If a transaction receives an error response, its word-aligned address must be recorded as having a fetch error.
- If a later transaction to the same address succeeds, the recorded error for that address must be cleared.

### 6.2 Internal Probing Mode

In internal probing mode, the scoreboard must observe instruction fetch results directly.

- If the fetch stage reports a fetch error, the failing address must be recorded.
- If the failing instruction is an uncompressed instruction that crosses a 32-bit boundary, and the error is on the second half of the instruction, the error must be recorded against the next word address.
- If a later successful fetch clears the error for an address, the record must be removed.
- For an uncompressed instruction crossing a 32-bit boundary, a successful fetch must clear error records for both containing word addresses.

The scoreboard must also observe PMP rejections of instruction fetches. PMP rejections must be tracked separately and must not be reported to the ISS as instruction-side bus errors. If an address has both a fetch-error record and a PMP-rejection record for the same fetch, the PMP rejection must suppress the bus-error notification.

### 6.3 Error Association with Retired Instructions

When an instruction becomes visible in the instruction decode stage, the scoreboard must determine whether it was fetched from an address with a recorded instruction-side bus error, excluding addresses with PMP-only rejections.

For an uncompressed instruction that is not word-aligned, the scoreboard must check both word addresses that the instruction spans.

If a relevant fetch-error record exists, the scoreboard must record a pending instruction-side error for that instruction, identified by the instruction’s sequence number.

Pending instruction-side error records must be consumed in sequence-number order when instructions retire:

- If an instruction with a pending error is flushed and never retires, its error record must be discarded when a later retired instruction is processed.
- If a retired instruction has a pending error record, the scoreboard must notify the ISS of the failing address before advancing the ISS for that instruction.

This ensures that the ISS generates an instruction-fault trap for exactly the instruction that experienced the fetch error.

## 7. Reporting and Cleanup

At the end of normal simulation, the scoreboard must report the total number of instructions that matched the ISS and then release the ISS session.

If simulation is terminated early, the scoreboard must still release the ISS session and perform any required cleanup.

The scoreboard must not leave a co-simulation session allocated after final phase or abort processing is complete.

# Core Ibex UVM Environment Behavioral Specification

## Overview

The core Ibex UVM environment is the top-level verification environment component for the Ibex core. It is responsible for assembling the verification infrastructure needed to run stimulus, collect interface activity, and support RTL/ISS co-simulation checking.

The environment itself must not generate stimulus, execute test sequences, or directly perform protocol checking. Instead, it must create, configure, and connect the child verification components that provide those behaviors.

## Configuration Requirements

The environment must obtain its configuration from the UVM configuration database. The required configuration must include:

- A general environment configuration object.
- A virtual clock/reset interface.
- A virtual DUT probe interface.

If any of these required configuration items cannot be retrieved, the environment must report a fatal UVM error and abort its initialization.

The retrieved virtual clock/reset interface and DUT probe interface must be made available through the environment configuration object so that child components can use them.

## Component Creation

The environment must instantiate the following components:

- A data memory interface response agent.
- An instruction memory interface response agent.
- An interrupt request agent.
- A co-simulation agent.
- A scrambling-key agent.
- A virtual sequencer.
- A scoreboard.

All components must be created as children of the environment so that their lifetimes and UVM phases are managed by the environment.

The scrambling-key agent must be provided with a configuration that selects device-side pull-agent behavior.

## Sequencer Access

The environment must make the sequencers of the data memory interface, instruction memory interface, and interrupt request agent accessible through the virtual sequencer. This allows virtual sequences to coordinate stimulus generation across all three interfaces through a single sequencer object.

## Memory Transaction Forwarding

The environment must forward observed data memory transactions to the co-simulation agent’s data-memory input path.

The environment must forward observed instruction memory transactions to the co-simulation agent’s instruction-memory input path.

These forwarded transaction streams must preserve the content and order of the transactions as they were observed on the respective interfaces.

## Scoreboard and Double-Fault Detection

The environment must instantiate a scoreboard.

If the environment configuration enables double-fault detection, the environment must forward retired-instruction information from the co-simulation agent to the scoreboard. This enables the scoreboard to observe instruction retirement activity and detect double-fault conditions.

If double-fault detection is not enabled, this retired-instruction forwarding path is not required.

## Reset Behavior

The environment shall provide a coordinated reset operation. When invoked, it must reset:

- The data-memory interface response agent.
- The instruction-memory interface response agent.
- The co-simulation agent.

Resetting the co-simulation agent must flush its pending observations and notify its internal scoreboard that the current ISS session must be terminated and reinitialized.

The environment reset operation does not itself reload the test binary. The controlling testbench reset sequence must reload the binary into the reinitialized ISS memory model before post-reset checking is resumed.

The environment is not required to reset the interrupt agent, scrambling-key agent, virtual sequencer, or the separate environment-level scoreboard directly.

## Boundary of Responsibility

The environment is an integration and configuration component. It must not alter memory transaction content, create interrupts, drive the DUT, or perform final pass/fail checking itself. Those responsibilities belong to the agents, sequences, and scoreboard that the environment creates and connects.
